issues.where: frames 1879–1895, on either side of the central sun reflection
issues.what: The dark coastal shapes fade under the brighter oblique view instead of tracking cleanly into it. The overlapping geography makes the descent read as a blend between views rather than a single flight.
issues.fix: Align the coastlines and cloud shadows in the same 3D camera move before blending, and carry the same light and exposure through the transition.

issues.where: frames 2120–2154, from the Caribbean to the full globe
issues.what: The rise looks like the dive played backward. The framing retraces the same landmarks, and the Cuban coastline and the large Pacific cloud spiral reappear in essentially the same configuration.
issues.fix: Give the climb a different heading or bank and keep clouds moving forward in time so the ascent reads as a continuation rather than a rewind.

issues.where: frames 1854–1879, bright cloud edges around the Gulf and Caribbean
issues.what: Some bright cloud details break into short, separated marks along the zoom direction instead of reading as one smooth streak.
issues.fix: Use more temporal samples along the camera path and check bright cloud edges at the fastest point of the dive.

issues.where: frames 1680–1829, the Pacific cloud spiral west of Mexico
issues.what: The hold shows slight globe drift, but the prominent cloud spiral appears pinned to the surface throughout.
issues.fix: Add subtle cloud advection independent of globe rotation while keeping the star field stable.
